quotes.text: Governance that isn't code is just a suggestion. If you're still relying on PDF policies and SharePoint checklists and email approvals, you have compliance theater, not compliance.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A sharp, memorable argument for automated governance instead of paper policies.

quotes.text: A control plane is the system that makes decisions about how other systems behave. It's the layer above execution. It's where intent is translated into policy.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a precise definition of the central concept of the episode.

quotes.text: Treat permissions as entropy generators, not rewards. Every time you grant access, you're adding entropy to the system. Design expiration into every access grant from the start.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Offers a concrete design principle against permission sprawl.

quotes.text: Stop counting apps. That's the wrong metric. Start counting technical debt surface area. The real question isn't how many power apps do we have.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes app proliferation as a maintenance and risk liability rather than a success metric.

quotes.text: If you cannot explain your Microsoft strategy in economic terms, you don't have a strategy. You have a shopping list.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the episode's demand to tie Microsoft spending to business outcomes.

takeaways: Licensing, permission sprawl, manual governance, app sprawl, ungoverned AI agents, builder bias and blanket E5 licensing compound into invisible waste in a Microsoft 365 tenant.
The root cause is a missing control plane: Entra ID should act as the backbone from which SharePoint, Teams, Purview, Defender and Copilot agents inherit policy.
A 90-day recovery of audit, governance automation and control plane design, sustained by clear ownership, decision rights and cadence, recovers license waste before renewals and price increases.
hook: Many organizations pay for Microsoft 365 E5 and Copilot yet leak money through unused licenses, orphaned apps, permission sprawl and governance that exists only on paper. This episode is for CIOs, CFOs and Microsoft 365 architects who need to justify their Microsoft spend. Learn the seven architecture sins, how to calculate your own leakage and a 90-day path to a governed control plane.
